parameters.content:
## ONE SWEEP A DAY, 10:00 IST
Reads the whole pipeline, works out who is overdue by grade, writes each buyer a follow-up with a genuinely new reason to reply, sends it as an approved template, then writes the touch back.

A lead due at 2pm waits until 10am tomorrow. That is deliberate: all outbound lands in one predictable window instead of pinging buyers at random hours, and one failed cron delays messages by a day rather than losing them.

## THE CADENCE
HOT every 3 days, WARM every 5, COLD every 21, JUNK never.
Hard stop at 6 automated follow-ups.

6 touches is a safety stop, not a target: WARM spans about a month, COLD about four. Most leads book, reply or get marked Lost long before it.

Skipped entirely: Booked, Lost, Dropped — and Engaged while the conversation is still live (last inbound under CONVERSATION_HOLD_HOURS). Nothing is more embarrassing than a scheduled nudge landing on top of a live chat.

## WHY THE WRITE-BACK MATTERS
`Update Touch Count` sets last_touch to now, so tomorrow's sweep sees this lead as freshly touched and skips it until the interval passes again.

If it fails silently the same lead gets messaged EVERY DAY — worse than the workflow not running at all. So it retries 3 times and, if it still fails, the error output alerts the sales manager instead of being swallowed.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Tune the cadence here and review it after a month of real data. These numbers are a starting point, not a law.

nodes.name: Find Follow-Ups Due
nodes.notes: Returns nothing when nobody is due, so the rest of the workflow simply does not run. No empty emails, no wasted API calls.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({
  model: $('Config').first().json.CLAUDE_MODEL,
  max_tokens: 2000,
  fallbacks: 'default',
  output_config: {
    effort: 'medium',
    format: { type: 'json_schema', schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        update_line: { type: 'string' },
        internal_note: { type: 'string' }
      },
      required: ['update_line', 'internal_note'],
      additionalProperties: false
    } }
  },
  system: 'You write the variable part of a WhatsApp follow-up for an Indian real estate developer.

The fixed approved template reads: "Hi {name}, an update on {project}: {update_line}" followed by View Details / Download Brochure / Schedule Visit buttons. You write update_line only.

Hard rules for update_line:
- ONE single line. No line breaks, no tabs, no bullet points, no emoji. Under 240 characters.
- It must carry ONE genuinely new reason to reply: a new unit or floor released, a price or possession update, a bank pre-approval or subvention offer, a weekend open house, a construction milestone, or a specific useful question.
- Never write "just following up", "gentle reminder", "checking in", or "did you get my message".
- Escalate VALUE as the follow-up number rises, never pressure. Follow-up 5 should be the most useful message, not the most desperate one.
- Do not invent a hard fact you were not given. Prefer a real question or a soft, honest offer over a fabricated price cut or a fake deadline.
- Match the grade: HOT gets specifics and urgency, WARM gets useful information, COLD gets low-commitment value.

internal_note is one short line for the sales manager explaining the angle you chose.',
  messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Follow-up ' + $json.followup_number + ' of ' + $json.max_followups + '
Name: ' + $json.name + '
Project: ' + $json.project + '
Grade: ' + $json.grade + '
Score: ' + ($json.score || 'n/a') + '
Budget: ' + ($json.budget || 'unknown') + '
Configuration: ' + ($json.configuration || 'unknown') + '
Timeline: ' + ($json.timeline || 'unknown') + '
Source: ' + $json.source + '
Days since last contact: ' + $json.days_since_touch + '
Last action they took: ' + ($json.last_action || 'none') + '
Original enquiry: ' + ($json.message || 'none') + '
What we know: ' + ($json.ai_summary || 'nothing yet') + '
Suggested next action: ' + ($json.next_action || 'none') } ]
}) }}

nodes.name: Claude - Write Follow-Up
nodes.notes: A fixed template would be simpler, but follow-up 5 saying the same thing as follow-up 2 is exactly why nurture sequences get muted. The approved template never changes - only the variable inside it does.

nodes.name: Sanitise Template Variable
nodes.notes: Runs once per item so each lead keeps its own copy.

nodes.name: WA - Send Follow-Up Template
nodes.notes: A lead who has not replied is outside the 24h window, so this must be an approved template. The buttons carry the same payloads as RE-00, so a tap drops the buyer straight back into the button flow.

nodes.name: Actually Delivered?
nodes.notes: Only burn a touch if Meta accepted the message. A rejected send must not cost the lead one of its six follow-ups.

nodes.name: Update Touch Count
nodes.notes: THE node that stops a daily repeat. Retries 3 times; if it still fails the error output raises an alarm instead of failing silently.
